thread:
priyanka: Heads-up — integration test flagged a weird response shape from /v1/responses. SDK v2 throws "parse error: expected object" when the server returns an empty array. Anyone seen this in prod?

ethan: Yep saw a flaky customer report earlier. They got `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8` and body `[]`. SDK expects top-level object with `outputs`.

maria: Do you have the raw response? can you paste it?

priyanka: Pasted from our logs: ```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8

[]
```

jonathan: Oof. Our contract (openapi/json-schema) for that endpoint is: ```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "outputs": { "type": "array" }
  },
  "required": ["outputs"]
}
```
So empty array is not allowed — server is returning the older legacy shape (top-level array) for some requests.

ethan: Which codepath? streaming vs non-streaming?

priyanka: Non-streaming, small payloads. Happens during fallback to model-variant `gen-legacy-v1` when cache miss + high load.

maria: Two options: 1) make server always wrap legacy arrays into `{ "outputs": [...] }` before sending, or 2) make SDK accept top-level arrays as backward-compatible.

jonathan: I prefer server-side fix for correctness, but SDK quick patch reduces customer impact. We should do both — SDK patch as compatibility shim, server fix in the next deploy.

priyanka: Agreed. SDK task is low-risk: if response is array, wrap in object and emit a debug log and metric `sdk.compat.wrap_array`.

ethan: I'll open a tiny PR in the sdk-js repo (will add unit + integration test). tagging @maria for server rollout plan.

maria: For server, I'll add middleware in the response pipeline that checks content-type + body for top-level arrays and transforms: ```js
if (contentType.includes('application/json') && Array.isArray(parsedBody)) {
  parsedBody = { outputs: parsedBody };
}
```
This will keep the canonical schema. We'll gate behind a feature-flag `wrap-legacy-array` and enable in canary.

jonathan: Also add a schema mismatch log with the route + model-variant so we can find any other legacy carriers. Add an alert if >100 mismatches/hour.

priyanka: Who will own the SDK shim PR? ethan? ETA?

ethan: I can do it today. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/432 (draft). Will wire the metric and a warning in console.

maria: Server PR est: tomorrow morning, will route a canary to `eng-playground` then roll to prod if no errors. I will also add a small e2e test to ensure Content-Type header with charset is handled (some parsers choke).

priyanka: Thanks. Quick checklist for the release notes: mention backward-compatibility shim in SDK, server normalization, and the new metric `response.schema.mismatch`. Also call out that clients should still prefer the stable object shape.

jonathan: One more: ensure SDK behavior is deterministic for streaming clients — if streaming NDJSON is used we must not wrap incremental events. So the shim should only apply for non-streaming 200 responses with a single JSON array.

ethan: Good point. I'll guard by `response.headers['transfer-encoding'] !== 'chunked'` and `content-type` check.

ci-bot: CI passed for sdk-js PR #432 (unit). Integration tests queued. :white_check_mark:

priyanka: Great. I'll file a short incident-like note in #incidents if the canary finds anything. Otherwise, we'll close this thread once server PR is merged and SDK patch is released. :thumbsup:
